scope: Bounded editorial synthesis of primary-source evidence through 2026-10-16; not exhaustive.
ranking_method: Editorial ordering by technical impact, precision of bottleneck, independent evidence convergence, observable milestone, and counterevidence; no synthetic weighted score.
paper3_outlook_semantics: Qualitative editorial outlook only; not calibrated probabilities, not model output, and not labels.

candidates.title: Joint KV-cache scheduling and speculative decoding under heterogeneous, changing load
candidates.precise_question: Under fixed accelerator-memory, output-quality, and tail-latency constraints, can a joint cache-retention/placement and speculative-execution policy improve end-to-end goodput over separately tuned policies for held-out changing request workloads?
candidates.strongest_baseline: KV-constrained scheduling has exact average-latency optimality in a semi-online model, constant regret under stochastic arrivals, and no constant competitive ratio in a fully adversarial online model; reported heterogeneous speculative decoding results remain configuration-specific.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Jointly account for cache residency, acceptance rate, accelerator contention, preemption, workload shift, and p95/p99 SLOs while holding output quality fixed.
supporting_evidence: Theoretical online/offline distinction is explicit in 2502.07115.
SPECTRE reports up to 2.28x in evaluated settings, not an externally replicated universal guarantee.
Independent cache eviction papers report quality/footprint trade-offs.
counterevidence_and_risks: Adversarial online constant-competitive guarantees are impossible in the cited model.
Component speedups may not compose; quality, memory, and tail latency can trade off.

paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Plausible if fixed-workload or fixed-cache assumptions fail in deployment.

candidates.potential_impact: High if it lowers serving cost or latency at unchanged output quality and SLO compliance.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Map one public serving stack's controls; preregister an equal-memory, equal-quality, held-out-arrival replay comparison. Recommendation only; not a validated optimal action.
candidates.objective_milestone: Independent implementation reproduces an end-to-end goodput or tail-latency gain on held-out arrivals while meeting fixed quality and memory constraints.
candidates.upgrade_if: Benefit survives matched memory, held-out workload, quality, and p95/p99 constraints with independent replication.
candidates.downgrade_if: Gain vanishes after equal-budget accounting, shifts cost to transfer/preemption, or harms output quality.
candidates.uncertainty: High; preprint claims and model/workload specificity limit transfer.

candidates.title: Repository-scale verified code generation and repair
candidates.subfield: Programming languages, software engineering, formal methods
candidates.precise_question: Can agents create patches satisfying explicit formal specifications and repository tests across unseen multi-file projects, with independent assurance that the specification matches intended behavior?
candidates.strongest_baseline: VeriSoftBench contains 500 repository-context Lean obligations; vericoding benchmark contains 12,504 Lean/Verus/Dafny specifications; SWE-Bench Pro has 1,865 repository tasks across 41 projects. These endpoints are distinct and their rates must not be pooled.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Transitive repository context, proof/spec completeness, issue-to-spec correspondence, and hidden regression detection.
supporting_evidence: VeriSoftBench reports poor transfer from Mathlib-style tasks and a benefit from dependency-closure context.
The vericoding benchmark shows substantial language- and task-family-dependent headroom.
SWE-Bench Pro provides held-out repository evaluation.
counterevidence_and_risks: Benchmark scores may reward incomplete specifications or visible tests.
Formal proof of a formalized statement does not establish the statement captures user intent.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; repository dependencies remain a bottleneck.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if proof success fails to transfer to real bug-free behavior.

candidates.potential_impact: Very high in correctness-critical software if patches are both useful and verified against intended behavior.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Build an endpoint taxonomy across theorem proof, verified synthesis, and repository repair; audit specification coverage before any matched evaluation.
candidates.objective_milestone: Higher independently reviewed issue-resolution rate on unseen repositories with hidden regression tests and audited spec-to-code correspondence.
candidates.upgrade_if: Gains replicate across held-out repositories and independent evaluators with no regression increase.
candidates.downgrade_if: Performance collapses under hidden tests, repository shift, or specification perturbation.
candidates.uncertainty: High; task distributions and correctness criteria differ substantially.

candidates.title: Artifact-level process verification for multi-agent execution
candidates.precise_question: Which intermediate verifier signals improve the probability of an independently validated correct final artifact over no verifier and simple deterministic checks, after accounting for verifier cost and false positives?
candidates.strongest_baseline: MAS-ProVe compares three verifier paradigms, two granularities, five verifiers, four context strategies, and six MAS frameworks; authors report inconsistent gains and high variance.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Reliable labels for trajectory correctness and prospective linkage from verifier decisions to independently checked final outcomes.
supporting_evidence: A broad 2026 empirical study directly reports that process verification does not consistently improve MAS performance.
counterevidence_and_risks: Verifier can reward persuasive traces rather than correctness.
Context length, verifier cost, and task mix confound apparent gains.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; no stable universal verifier result.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Plausible if process-level scores fail to predict artifact correctness.

candidates.potential_impact: High if verification can safely guide agents on long, expensive tasks.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Freeze verifier decisions before outcome checks; design a prospective paired task study with false-positive costs and task-family grouping.
candidates.objective_milestone: Replicated increase in independently checked task completion over no-verifier and deterministic baselines, net of added compute/context.
candidates.upgrade_if: Positive results replicate across task families and verifiers with calibrated false-positive rates.
candidates.downgrade_if: Gains are unstable, judge-dependent, or disappear after cost and artifact validation.
candidates.uncertainty: High; current source reports variance and inconsistent effects.

candidates.title: Tight, certified filters for fully adaptive differential privacy
candidates.precise_question: Can valid, tight, numerically certified filters be constructed for fully adaptive composition beyond currently covered sampling regimes, with explicit assumptions and runtime/error guarantees?
candidates.strongest_baseline: The 2026 f-DP filter paper disproves the naive natural filter in general, characterizes validity, and gives an approximate GDP filter for subsampled Gaussian mechanisms at q<0.2 and q>0.8.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Intermediate sampling rates and implementation-grade certified error bounds for a narrowly specified mechanism family.
supporting_evidence: A source-verified theorem identifies both a failed natural construction and regime-limited approximate alternatives.
counterevidence_and_risks: A practical gain may be dominated by existing RDP or privacy-loss-distribution accountants.
Theorem assumptions may not match deployed adaptive mechanisms.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Plausible for restricted parameter regimes, uncertain generally.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if current assumed adaptivity model is too broad or too narrow.

candidates.potential_impact: High where tighter valid accounting enables more useful private analyses.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Map theorem assumptions to code and identify an exact uncovered parameter interval before implementation; no run performed.
candidates.objective_milestone: Independent proof/code certificate gives a sound tighter bound than a pinned baseline on a prespecified mechanism family.
candidates.upgrade_if: Formal error enclosure and matched privacy-utility comparison pass independent review.
candidates.downgrade_if: No certified advantage over established accountants or assumptions fail on target use cases.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium-high; theorem boundary is clear but practical impact is not evaluated.

candidates.title: Scientific agents that move from ideas to independently verified evidence
candidates.subfield: AI for science, multi-agent systems, metascience
candidates.precise_question: Can an agent system generate a frozen falsifiable question and execute a discriminating study whose provenance, raw evidence, and conclusion survive independent adjudication?
candidates.strongest_baseline: EIG reports proposal-quality benchmark gains; a 2026 historical-backtesting protocol reports an astronomy pilot and freezes a prospective set; neither establishes broad autonomous scientific discovery.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Outcome taxonomy reliability, prior-art checking, execution provenance, and the transition from proposal scores to actual independently reproducible results.
supporting_evidence: Evolving idea-graph systems expose claims/conflicts and proposal editing.
A separate historical-backtesting paper provides a prospective falsifiable evaluation frame.
counterevidence_and_risks: Proposal quality is not truth or executed evidence.
Human outcome labels in a recent pilot had low agreement, making the target itself noisy.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Low-confidence; general autonomous discovery remains unvalidated.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if idea scores fail to predict independent evidence yield.

candidates.potential_impact: Potentially transformative, but only if agents reliably produce new verified evidence rather than fluent plans.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Compare evaluation protocols and establish label-adjudication reliability before prospectively scoring systems.
candidates.objective_milestone: On a frozen future cohort, systems improve independently adjudicated executed-evidence outcomes over simple baselines.
candidates.upgrade_if: Blinded labels are reliable and held-out executed outcomes replicate with raw artifacts.
candidates.downgrade_if: Label disagreement, missingness, or proposal-only outputs prevent objective evaluation.
candidates.uncertainty: Very high; impact large, evidence is mostly proposal and protocol development.

candidates.title: Conflict-aware persistent memory for multi-agent systems
candidates.subfield: Agent systems, knowledge representation, AI reliability
candidates.precise_question: Does explicit claim-status and contradiction handling improve downstream correctness and update behavior over ordinary retrieval, merge, debate, or judge baselines on long-lived tasks?
candidates.strongest_baseline: LatticeMind reports 0.97 versus 0.61 on its label-blind ConflictBank comparison; its four secondary planning benchmarks are mixed and the conflict benchmark is small.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: External replication, scale and domain transfer, temporal updates, and correctness under evidence that later reverses earlier claims.
supporting_evidence: A 2026 primary preprint evaluates symbolic conflict checking and selective reconciliation.
counterevidence_and_risks: The main benchmark is a bounded construct; secondary tasks do not uniformly improve.
Accuracy on conflict classification may not transfer to long-horizon task success.

paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Plausible if benchmark conflict handling does not improve downstream work.

candidates.potential_impact: Medium-high if persistent systems become more reliable under contradictory updates.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Track independent replication and require a downstream task endpoint with time-ordered evidence updates.
candidates.objective_milestone: External study shows higher downstream accuracy and safe supersession rates than retrieval/merge baselines.
candidates.upgrade_if: Replication across larger, independent datasets and long tasks confirms benefit.
candidates.downgrade_if: Effect is benchmark-specific or reconciliation introduces harmful false overrides.
candidates.uncertainty: High; one recent preprint and narrow main benchmark.

candidates.title: KV-cache eviction and retention with explicit quality guarantees
candidates.precise_question: For pinned model/workload families, how much KV memory can be removed while maintaining a prespecified quality and tail-latency envelope, including long-context and distribution-shift conditions?
candidates.strongest_baseline: Recent global and re-formulated eviction approaches report cache reductions with maintained or improved task performance on evaluated benchmarks; results are author-reported and benchmark-specific.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Quality tail-risk under long-context, model changes and workload shift; cache savings must be measured end-to-end rather than token retention alone.
supporting_evidence: Two 2026 preprints propose distinct global/cache eviction rules and report benchmark evaluations.
counterevidence_and_risks: Averages can conceal rare long-context failures.
Model, prompt, and decode distributions can invalidate eviction rankings.

paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Plausible if quality does not track local salience estimates.

candidates.potential_impact: High if large memory reductions preserve quality and SLA at serving scale.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Audit benchmark and prompt overlap; define a fixed quality non-inferiority margin and a held-out long-context stress set.
candidates.objective_milestone: Independent reproduction shows reduced peak memory at a prespecified non-inferior quality margin and no tail regression.
candidates.upgrade_if: Results replicate on unseen models and long-context workloads.
candidates.downgrade_if: Savings depend on prompt-specific tuning or hide rare severe quality regressions.
candidates.uncertainty: High; rapid method turnover and limited external replication.

candidates.title: Runtime KV placement across heterogeneous memory tiers
candidates.precise_question: Can an online placement policy exploit HBM plus off-package/host memory bandwidth to increase inference goodput under capacity, transfer, and tail-latency constraints?
candidates.strongest_baseline: A 2025 source formulates dynamic KV placement and derives a theoretical upper bound, while explicitly not supplying a concrete scheduling policy.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Real transfer contention, page movement, prompt-specific access frequency, and interaction with compute scheduling.
supporting_evidence: Heterogeneous memory links are increasingly available; source analysis identifies theoretical headroom.
counterevidence_and_risks: Upper-bound headroom is not achievable-policy evidence.
Data movement may erase capacity advantages and worsen tail latency.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; policy gap needs systems implementation.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if transfer cost dominates expected bandwidth gain.

candidates.potential_impact: High if it enables larger models/batches on a fixed accelerator budget.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Derive a workload-specific cost model from a public runtime before selecting a placement policy.
candidates.objective_milestone: Implementable policy improves throughput at matched memory and tail-latency constraints over static placement.
candidates.upgrade_if: Policy gains survive realistic interconnect and contention measurements.
candidates.downgrade_if: Bound is loose or migrations dominate the service workload.
candidates.uncertainty: High; current evidence is primarily formulation and bound.

candidates.title: Formal verification across realistic repository dependency closures
candidates.precise_question: Can proof automation scale across multi-file, definition-rich repositories while maintaining soundness and reducing the human time needed to discharge real software obligations?
candidates.strongest_baseline: VeriSoftBench's 500-task repository-level Lean suite reports dependency-closure difficulty and improvement from curated relevant context; vericoding adds cross-language specifications but with distinct task semantics.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Large dependency closures, context selection, proof maintenance under code changes, and adequacy of formal specifications.
supporting_evidence: New repository-scale benchmark makes a previously underrepresented setting measurable.
counterevidence_and_risks: Benchmark construction and repository selection may not represent production verification.
Passing obligations does not show total verification coverage.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; progress likely incremental and domain-specific.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if context reduction or automation fails at scale.

candidates.potential_impact: Very high if real codebases gain maintainable, sound proof coverage at lower cost.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Track benchmark extensions and independent Lean/Verus repository evaluations; keep proof completion and intended-behavior correctness separate.
candidates.objective_milestone: More real repository obligations discharged per expert-hour with sound checking and maintained proofs after code edits.
candidates.upgrade_if: External teams reproduce gains on new repositories and measure maintenance cost.
candidates.downgrade_if: Proofs depend on narrow benchmark context or break under routine code evolution.
candidates.uncertainty: High; objective metrics exist but deployment transfer is unknown.

candidates.title: Long-horizon software engineering agents on held-out repositories
candidates.precise_question: Do agents resolve multi-hour or multi-day maintenance issues on unseen repositories with correct patches, low regression rates, and independent human acceptance?
candidates.strongest_baseline: SWE-Bench Pro supplies a larger, more difficult repository task suite with held-out settings; the paper reports that strong systems still solve a minority under its protocol.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Long dependency chains, changing state, test coverage, tool reliability, and evaluation cost/acceptance criteria.
supporting_evidence: The benchmark explicitly targets more complex software engineering tasks and held-out repositories.
counterevidence_and_risks: Benchmark success may not transfer to live maintenance.
Task selection and test suites can encode a narrow notion of completion.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; task scope grows faster than current reliability evidence.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Possible if solved benchmarks do not predict deployed acceptance.

candidates.potential_impact: High if agents safely reduce expert effort on substantial maintenance.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Use task-level accepted patch outcomes and held-out repositories; audit whether issue, tests, and maintainers agree.
candidates.objective_milestone: Replicated growth in accepted, regression-free patches on held-out repositories with controlled tool budgets.
candidates.upgrade_if: Independent maintainers accept patches and gains persist under hidden tests and realistic budgets.
candidates.downgrade_if: Performance is scaffold-specific or causes security/maintenance regressions.
candidates.uncertainty: High; test endpoint is clearer than transfer to practice.

candidates.title: AI/software supply-chain risk measured against confirmed incidents
candidates.precise_question: Do concrete provenance and policy controls reduce independently confirmed compromise or vulnerability introduction in AI-enabled software supply chains without unacceptable false blocks?
candidates.strongest_baseline: A recent study retrieves and classifies hundreds of thousands of discussions and manually analyzes a smaller thematic sample; it is a taxonomy/discourse analysis, not an incident-rate or causal-effect estimate.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: Linking artifacts and policy decisions to confirmed security outcomes with attribution, exposure denominators, and false-positive costs.
supporting_evidence: Large public discourse corpus indicates active concerns and offers a vocabulary for measurement.
counterevidence_and_risks: Discussion volume is not prevalence or impact.
Impact-label inter-rater agreement and incident attribution are difficult.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Uncertain; incident evidence is sparse and delayed.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Plausible if concern taxonomies do not track verified incidents.

candidates.potential_impact: High if controls measurably reduce confirmed compromise while retaining developer utility.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Define incident-confirmation and denominator protocol; link software artifacts and advisories rather than relying on discussion labels.
candidates.objective_milestone: Prospective matched evaluation reports confirmed incidents, exposure, false blocks, and independent adjudication.
candidates.upgrade_if: Reliable artifact-to-incident linkage and a feasible control evaluation emerge.
candidates.downgrade_if: Data cannot support attribution or only proxy discourse outcomes are available.
candidates.uncertainty: Very high; outcome observability and causal attribution are weak.

candidates.title: Instance-adaptive incremental view maintenance beyond fixed query-optimal thresholds
candidates.precise_question: Can a workload-sensitive choice among valid incremental-view-maintenance configurations lower actual end-to-end cost under changing distributions after including exactness, migration, memory, and delay?
candidates.strongest_baseline: The 2026 heavy-light IVM source already handles changing heavy/light membership and database-size changes with amortized rebalancing; it selects query-optimal fixed epsilon against worst degree configurations.
candidates.unresolved_bottleneck: No proven online selection rule has demonstrated net benefit over the fixed minimax baseline once migration and memory costs are included.
supporting_evidence: A source-level theorem gives a clear asymptotic update baseline and explicit rebalancing.
counterevidence_and_risks: Broad dynamic-skew challenge is already covered.
Naive switching/rebuild can lose a factor proportional to database size on alternating regimes.

paper3_outlook.direct_resolution: Low confidence for current formulation; prior art closes the broad claim.
paper3_outlook.premise_revision: Likely required if no objective advantage survives migration accounting.

candidates.potential_impact: Potentially high for workloads with severe shifts, but no novel benefit is established.
candidates.paper4_recommended_action: Do not activate a task unless a precise workload model and migration-aware advantage conjecture survive source review.
candidates.objective_milestone: A source-supported algorithm proves or measures lower total amortized cost than the fixed-epsilon baseline under an explicit shift model.
candidates.upgrade_if: A nontrivial migration-correct theorem and executable comparator are identified.
candidates.downgrade_if: No advantage beyond existing rebalancing can be shown.
candidates.uncertainty: High; present candidate is deliberately down-ranked after prior-art correction.

clusters.name: Inference systems
clusters.bottleneck: Joint memory, compute, output quality and tail-SLO behavior.
clusters.milestone: Equal-budget held-out workload gain with independent reproduction.
clusters.disconfirming_evidence: Component gains fail to compose or shift cost into transfer and tail latency.

clusters.name: Trustworthy software agents
clusters.bottleneck: Correct issue-to-spec-to-patch correspondence and independent artifact validation.
clusters.milestone: Held-out repositories, hidden regression tests, audited specifications, accepted patches.
clusters.disconfirming_evidence: Benchmark gains disappear under hidden tests or formal specifications do not capture intended behavior.

clusters.name: Autonomous science
clusters.bottleneck: Reliable labels and traceable transition from proposal to executed evidence.
clusters.milestone: Frozen prospective cohort, reliable blinded adjudication, reproducible results.
clusters.disconfirming_evidence: Label disagreement, missingness, or proposal-only success prevents objective scoring.

clusters.name: Private adaptive computation
clusters.bottleneck: Tightness plus rigorous numerical certification under realistic adaptivity.
clusters.milestone: Independent proof/code certificate with matched baseline and assumptions.
clusters.disconfirming_evidence: Existing accountants dominate or assumptions do not match deployed mechanisms.

system_integration.decision: Editorial ranking only; no successor task admitted by this report.
